label: PF Backlog 589
title: EDP-08: Versioned migration framework + DB role separation (owner/runtime/read/backup) + schema-ownership policy (no auto-migrate on startup)
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.

brief.problem: Application startup may auto-migrate the database schema, and all database operations use a single superuser role — unacceptable for enterprise.
brief.what_adds: Versioned migration runner, four-scoped DB roles, and a fail-closed startup gate that refuses to run with an outdated schema.
brief.why: Prevents privilege escalation via database compromise and ensures schema changes are auditable and reversible.
brief.who_feels: Security teams (least-privilege), DBAs (controlled schema changes), SREs (deterministic deployments).

objective: Implement a versioned migration framework in Go with four-tier DB role separation and a schema-ownership policy that prevents auto-migration on application startup.
acceptance_criteria: Migration runner applies versioned SQL migrations with embedded files and checksum verification
Four DB roles (owner/runtime/read/backup) created with scoped GRANTs via migration
Application startup fails closed if schema version is behind expected
Integration tests run migrations against PostgreSQL in CI
Schema-ownership policy documented in config/guardrail-policy.json
in_scope: Initial migration creating four DB roles with scoped GRANTs
approach: Define migration directory structure, implement checksummed runner, create roles migration, add startup gate, write integration tests against PostgreSQL.
verification: Startup with out-of-date schema returns 503 error
Four roles verified via \du in integration test
No auto-migrate path exists (code review + test)
risks: Role separation must be tested against actual PostgreSQL; local dev may bypass
Versioned migrations with branching teams risk merge conflicts on version numbers
No-auto-migrate policy may break existing dev workflows if not gated early
rollback: Revert migrations package and startup gate; existing schema remains unchanged if no production migrations have run.
evidence: core/change_policy.py and config/guardrail-policy.json show policy-as-code pattern
Language rule confirms Go-only for new code
No existing migration tooling detected in candidate list

analysis.implementation_strategy: Create Go package `internal/migrations/` with versioned migration runner using embedded SQL files. Define four DB roles (owner, runtime, read-only, backup) as migration steps creating PostgreSQL roles with scoped GRANTs. Implement schema-ownership policy: app startup checks migration version and refuses to run if out of date; no auto-migrate. Leverage config/verification-policy.json and config/artifact-owners.json patterns for role ownership metadata.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-1293 (architecture ADR) — DB role model must align with ADR
REQUIRES BI-PF-1299 (storage interfaces) — migration store interface may be consumed
RELATED BI-PF-1297 (Policy Registry) — schema-ownership mirrors versioned policy pattern
conflict_findings: BI-PF-1299 creates internal/storage/ package; migrations package should depend on it, not duplicate
BI-PF-1297 policy registry may be the enforcement point for schema-ownership — coordinate
duplication_findings: No existing Go migration framework in candidate components
core/change_policy.py provides a policy pattern that can inform migration approval gates
config/guardrail-policy.json could host schema-ownership policy declarations
analysis.rationale: Database schema ownership and role separation are non-negotiable for the enterprise roadmap. No existing Go migration framework exists; a new package is required.
assumptions: CI has access to a real PostgreSQL instance for integration tests
Existing app startup has no current migration logic to preserve
risks: Role separation must be tested against actual PostgreSQL; local dev may bypass
Versioned migrations with branching teams risk merge conflicts on version numbers
No-auto-migrate policy may break existing dev workflows if not gated early
evidence: core/change_policy.py and config/guardrail-policy.json show policy-as-code pattern
Language rule confirms Go-only for new code
No existing migration tooling detected in candidate list
missing_info: Exact set of PostgreSQL GRANTs per role — needs security review
How dev environments handle migrations (docker-compose integration?)

missing: PostgreSQL role GRANT matrix needs security review
context_review.reason: Well-scoped new Go package with clear PostgreSQL integration; dependent on ADR (1293) for role model alignment but technically independent.
